In summary, our research is concerned with
developing radiation tolerant Gb/s optical links which can be used in the front-end readout of the ATLAS liquid Argon calorimeter.
developing radiation-tolerant links for use in the front-end readout of the ATLAS Liquid Argon Calorimeter (LAr) for the High-Luminosity Large Hadron Collider (HL-LHC).
the development of radiation-tolerant Gb/s optical links for the front-end readout of the ATLAS Liquid Argon Calorimeter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Gb/s links are radiation tolerant.

the link components are radiation tolerant up to the dose levels required in the ATLAS experiment (up to a few 10^16 n/cm^2) with a negligible impact on the link performance and the radiation tolerance of the link components is sufficient for the ATLAS experiment.
the G-Link based links can withstand the expected radiation levels at ATLAS with no significant performance degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that GLink links are radiation tolerant to the levels required to operate in the ATLAS liquid Argon Calorimeter environment and that the GLink links can be operated in a radiation environment at rates of at least 1.5 Gb/s.
all of the components studied appear to be suitable for the ATLAS LAr calorimeter readout system.
we are able to demonstrate that a complete G-Link link demonstrator is radiation hard to a fluence of 1.4x10 15 neutrons cm -2.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a complete link, including the VCSEL’s, the graded-index fibre and the GLink serialiser, can withstand a dose of 1.2 x 1015 n eq / cm2 (1 MeV neutron equivalent) and still operate at a bit error rate of 10-12.
the G-Link based link demonstrators are able to withstand neutron fluences up to 10^14 n/cm2 and that the link components can withstand ionising fluences up to ~10^16 n/cm2.

the GLink link demonstrator is radiation tolerant to at least 1.5x1015 n/cm2 (1 MeV equivalent neutrons) and that the VCSEL’s and optical fibres are tolerant to 1.5×1015 n/cm (1 MeV neutrons) and 5×1014 p/cm2 (10 MeV protons) respectively.
